log fix-184: dev-spawned bodies (~devNN) are not part of a save (DevNpcs adds their defs at runtime), so the post-load checks of fix-180 read - for every one, placed corpses after a load: fix80_corpse, fix163_sunk_body
notes: corpsepose = summary (shown motion key, dead/lies/shown flags, Animator on, pelvis, legs, root tilt, rest info). corpselegs = the most upright hind leg's angle from straight down (standing ~0-25 deg, lying 45-90). corpsepelvis = Spine_Spine_1 above the ground (a standing deer ~1 m). corpsefooting = the relief footing's state on the body ('off' when let go, '-' without footing). Run it with the relief on and off (G3TerrainRelief.SetOption). fix-184 (regress-1021b): humanoid ragdolls (orc, slave) settle with legs 30-40 deg off upright on flat ground (Orc 37.9), on the 18-33 deg Nordmar slope a ragdoll's pelvis rests up to 0.8 m over the ground and a creature's lying pose dips up to 0.25 m into the upslope side (deer -0.19): the slope bounds are wider. fix-221: a ragdoll is no longer lifted by its skin (feet in the uphill slope propped it, pelvis 0.6-0.7 m): humanoid slope pelvis <=0.5, corpsegap of a ragdoll = its collision parts' lowest clearance. fix-232: the slope's 'right' spawns (IceWolf dist 3, Orc dist 6) landed at (446.3,178.3,1080.2): 0.2-0.7 m from the foot of a 10 m rock face (x >= 446.5, ground 178 -> 183 -> 190 within 1 m), not on the slope: the wolf was tilted onto the face (survey plane 68 deg, capped 35) and lifted (pelvis 1.07), the orc's legs hung down the face (12 deg); now fixed spots on the 15-20 deg slope (IceWolf 444.5,1078.5, Orc 441.5,1081.0). corpselegs is measured from the ground's inward normal (CorpseRest survey), not world down: a wolf lying on a 35 deg slope with its legs downhill read 27 deg off world down. CorpseRest drops samples on a rock face (steeper than 45 deg from a pose corpse's floor) and retries missed rays from 3 m higher.
